comments.note: ProvisioningToolsViewModel.RunProvisioningAsync() and ShellViewModel.ProvisionAsync() both independently invoke IExternalToolProvisioner.EnsureAsync(). In production, one caller will redundantly download/verify if both run. The view-model should either signal back to the shell (callback/event) or the shell should delegate its orchestration through the view-model. Deferred to a later WP.

FakeExternalToolProvisioner is duplicated across 4 test files (DatabaseConnectorViewModelTests, MainWindowViewModelTests, LogonViewModelTests, PasswordSetupViewModelTests) due to the project's inline-fakes pattern. A shared TestHelpers or Fixtures file in VideoIndexer.App.Tests could eliminate this repetition.

CompositeArchiveExtractor is registered via a factory lambda to avoid DI constructor-selection ambiguity. Consider marking the 2-parameter constructor with [ActivatorUtilitiesConstructor] or restructuring to use a single constructor to make DI registration straightforward without the lambda workaround.

comments.note: AC #3 spec mentions 'AlreadyPresent or Downloaded' result values but IExternalToolProvisioner.EnsureAsync returns ToolPaths on success and throws on failure — there is no result-code enum. ShellViewModel.ProvisionAsync correctly handles any non-throwing return as success. The test covers this path. The AC wording is a holdover from an earlier design; the implementation is correct.

StaleCodeCoverage incremental-build files (.msCoverageSourceRootsMapping_*) were locked from a prior test run, causing a false-positive MSB3492 build error on first attempt. Deleted the two stale files; subsequent build succeeded cleanly. This is a pre-existing CI hygiene issue unrelated to WP-010.

No test currently validates that ProvisionAsync transitions through ProvisioningTools state before reaching Connecting (i.e. StateChanged events are not asserted). Since the state machine is deterministic and the start state is asserted in Constructor_InitialState_IsProvisioningTools, this is low risk, but an event-sequence assertion would add defence against future refactors.

comments.note: ProvisioningToolsViewModel.ProvideManually() doc-comment and inline comment both say 'deferred to WP-010', but this is WP-010. The stub comment should reference the correct future WP number. File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/ProvisioningToolsViewModel.cs, line ~100-106.

ShellViewModel.ProvisionAsync() calls EnsureAsync(null, ct) with null progress — no progress data reaches ProvisioningToolsViewModel. ProvisioningToolsViewModel.StartAsync() calls EnsureAsync independently for its own progress display. Until WP-015 wires the shell view and decides which path owns the transition, there are two independent EnsureAsync call sites. The developer and QA flagged this; it is deferred but reviewer concurs it should be resolved before the view wiring WP ships.

FakeExternalToolProvisioner is duplicated verbatim in 5 test files (ShellViewModelTests, DatabaseConnectorViewModelTests, PasswordSetupViewModelTests, MainWindowViewModelTests, LogonViewModelTests). If IExternalToolProvisioner gains parameters, all 5 copies need updating. A shared TestHelpers.cs or Fixtures project in VideoIndexer.App.Tests would eliminate this fragility. Previously noted by Developer and QA; reviewer concurs this should be addressed in a future test-hygiene WP.
